author: Mary McGuire
title: Warrant: Suspected cocaine found in car from Brooklyn Center crash that killed 6-year-old - NewsBreak
text:
By Mary McGuire ,
10 hours ago A search warrant is revealing new details about the driver in a deadly minibike crash in Brooklyn Center.
Last Thursday, 6-year-old Dreme Williams was killed, and a 10-year-old girl was seriously injured when the minibike they were riding was struck by a driver near the intersection of Brooklyn Drive and 63rd Avenue North.
Dreme Williams GoFundMe
Authorities said they were riding the minibike on the road and that there were no stop signs at the intersection.
In a search warrant application filed on Tuesday, an investigator with the Brooklyn Center Police Department asked for permission to take a blood sample from the driver, a 49-year-old woman, because authorities suspect she was under the influence of a controlled substance at the time of the crash.
In an interview with detectives, the driver said she didn’t remember the events leading up to the collision, nor did she know why she didn’t see the kids on the minibike. She also denied drinking alcohol.
“A look inside her vehicle pursuant to plain view at the scene revealed a substance that appears to be cocaine in the driver’s seat,” the search warrant application states.
The woman was given a breath test at the scene and blew a .000%. A detective also described the woman as “understandably hysterical” following the crash and said she was not able to tell them what happened.
An online fundraiser is collecting donations to help pay for funeral expenses. As of Wednesday afternoon, the GoFundMe page has raised more than $7,000.
“Dreme had her whole life ahead of her, and our family was not prepared to say goodbye,” the online fundraiser says. “She was only six. She should still be here making us laugh, celebrating birthdays, going to school, playing, growing, and creating memories with the people who loved her.”
At last check, the other girl involved in the collision was in critical but stable condition.
Bring Me The News does not typically name suspects until they have been formally charged with a crime.
